Documents and events

Timeline

From 1999 to 2026: negotiations, readiness checks and political targets. Events run from newest to oldest. Open an entry for details, its significance and sources.

Preparations are documented from 1999. Early evaluations took place in 2006, the current cycle began in 2019, and Cyprus joined SIS in 2023. Where a source gives only a month or period, no exact day is assumed.

22NOV 2026ProcedureGrade ACommission prepares an information item for the December Council

Event 22 November 2026 · Tracked since 27 November 2026

ST 15799/26 concerns the Justice and Home Affairs Council meeting on 3–4 December and is titled as an update on the application of the Schengen acquis in Cyprus. It is listed under Any Other Business. Access to the text is restricted.

Why it matters

Preparation of a briefing for ministers is confirmed. An information item is not a draft decision on full accession and does not itself confirm a vote.

Source and publication date

Source status: metadata for a restricted document. Austrian Parliament, ST 15799/26: created 22.11.2026, received by Parliament 23.11.2026.

Austrian Parliament · ST 15799/26 Council of the EU · meeting of 3 December
22NOV 2026PoliticsGrade CMedia commentary on Poland's position emerges

Event: 22 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 23 November 2026

A Kathimerini/KNEWS columnist named Poland among countries that might be cautious in a vote. The 22 November column also mentioned Austria and the Netherlands. It supplied no official Warsaw statement or text of a reservation.

Why it matters

Poland's public statements merit monitoring. There is no basis yet to conclude that it will veto accession.

Kathimerini / KNEWS · column on Schengen readiness
20NOV 2026Technical readinessGrade A / CTender opens for passport-control booths in Larnaca and Paphos

Event 20 November 2026 · Tracked since 25 November 2026

Tender MTCW/AIR2/BOOTHS/2026 was published with an estimated value of €440,000 and a 21 December submission deadline. Philenews reported 22 booths and eight months for manufacture, installation and testing after contract signature. The procurement entry gives an overall contract duration of 20 months.

Why it matters

The tender confirms further infrastructure upgrades. The different periods refer to different descriptions of the work; no link between completion and a mandatory accession date has been established.

Source and publication date

Official tender entry, published 20.11.2026 at 15:29; Philenews, description of equipment and work stages, 25.11.2026.

Cyprus eProcurement · MTCW/AIR2/BOOTHS/2026 Phileleftheros · airport equipment
20NOV 2026PoliticsGrade BEU and UK reaffirm work on the bases protocol

Event 20 November 2026 · Tracked since 24 November 2026

The summit's joint statement committed to completing implementation of the protocol on the British Sovereign Base Areas in Cyprus in all its parts.

Why it matters

This matters for the island's special arrangements. The statement establishes neither separate arrangements for Schengen checks at crossing points nor Cyprus's accession date.

Source and publication date

UK–EU Summit 2026 Joint Statement, 20.11.2026, point 5.

UK government · summit statement Council of the EU · ST 16174/26, point 5 EU–UK Joint Committee · 10 November
20NOV 2026PoliticsGrade A / CEU and Türkiye discuss a Cyprus settlement

Event: 20 November 2026 · Added to monitoring: 21 November 2026

Commission Executive Vice-President Raffaele Fitto met Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan in Ankara. The Turkish Foreign Ministry confirmed the meeting. CNA and Anadolu placed different emphasis on links between a Cyprus settlement and EU–Türkiye relations.

Why it matters

This is diplomatic context. No direct link to the Council's Schengen decision has been established.

Turkish Foreign Ministry · Fidan–Fitto meeting Cyprus News Agency · Commission position Anadolu · Fidan's position
18NOV 2026PoliticsGrade BGreek Prime Minister supports the 1 July 2027 target

Event 18 November 2026 · Tracked since 20 November 2026

In Nicosia, Kyriakos Mitsotakis expressed hope for Cyprus's formal accession on 1 July, at the start of Greece's Council presidency in the second half of 2027.

Why it matters

A specific target gained public backing from Athens. In the transcript, it is an expectation rather than an announcement of an adopted Council decision.

Source and publication date

Official transcript from the Greek Prime Minister; event and publication 18.11.2026.

Greek Prime Minister · Nicosia transcript

CM 4999/26 for the Council on 3–4 December lists Schengen governance issues, but no separate adoption of a Cyprus accession decision. Information item ST 15799/26 appeared later.

The initial agenda did not confirm an accession vote. Its contents could change before the meeting.

Event 13 November 2026

The agenda included Commission presentation of draft ST 14872/26, discussion and possible agreement. Separate updates from the Commission and Cyprus on full application of Schengen rules were also scheduled.

The planned subject of discussion is confirmed. ‘Possible agreement’ does not mean agreement was reached.

09NOV 2026PoliticsGrade ACommunity leaders agree on new crossings

Event: 9 November 2026

Two additional Green Line crossings were agreed under UN mediation. On 9 November, the UN named Louroujina–Lympia and Kambos–Karavostasi. The statement gave no opening dates.

Why it matters

The agreement supports intercommunal dialogue. Schengen entry and exit records remain a separate issue.

UN · statement on new crossings
27OCT 2026ProcedureGrade ADraft closure of action plans in six areas is registered

Event 27 October 2026

ST 14872/26 appeared in the Council register under file 2026/0337(NLE). The proposal concerns closure of plans on data protection, return, external borders, police, visas and SIS. The text is restricted.

Why it matters

The Commission proposed completing monitoring of the remedial plans. Registration of the proposal does not establish adoption and does not replace the decision on full Schengen application.

Source and publication date

Source status: proposal. Council of the EU, register entry for ST 14872/26, 27.10.2026.

Council of the EU · draft ST 14872/26
10OCT 2026Technical readinessGrade B / CMinister describes six remaining actions

Event 10 October 2026

In a CyBC interview, Ioannides expected six remaining actions to be completed by early November and full accession in 2027. The plan was then to notify the Commission and proceed through the subsequent institutional steps.

Why it matters

The statement clarifies the authorities' plan, but differs from the 1 October wording on how complete the work was. Six actions cannot automatically be equated with the six evaluation areas.

Source and publication date

CyBC, interview with Ioannides, published 10.10.2026.

RIK · Ioannides interview
07OCT 2026PoliticsGrade BMED9 supports Cyprus's progress

Event 7 October 2026

In the Split Declaration, MED9 countries welcomed the positive outcome of the 2025/2026 country report and the start of Council discussions. They called for timely completion of the remaining steps.

Why it matters

Collective political support was recorded. This wording set no specific accession date.

Source and publication date

Full text of the Split Declaration, 07.10.2026, Migration and Protection of the EU’s External Borders section; excerpts published by the Cyprus Presidency.

Full MED9 declaration MED9 group · Split declaration
04OCT 2026ProcedureGrade AReport on implementation of remedial action plans is prepared

Event 4 October 2026

The ST 13957/26 entry describes an assessment of implementation of plans addressing deficiencies identified in the 2021/2022/2023 initial evaluation. Access to the full text is restricted.

Formal monitoring of the plans is confirmed. The title does not establish the outcome of each recommendation.

Source and publication date

Source status: metadata for a restricted document. Austrian Parliament, ST 13957/26: created 04.10.2026, received by Parliament 09.10.2026. This differs from 5 October in the site's earlier selection; the creation date in the official entry is used here.

01OCT 2026PoliticsGrade BCyprus says Commission recommendations have been implemented

Event 1 October 2026

Nicholas Ioannides said the Commission's recommendations were considered implemented, Cyprus was technically ready and political agreement was now needed.

Why it matters

This was the government's official position. It cannot be substituted for an adopted Council act closing the action plans.

Source and publication date

EUAA, account of the statement with an event date of 01.10.2026; Cyprus government announcement. The government announcement was published on 02.10.2026.

15SEP 2026ProcedureGrade ACountry report appears in Council working party materials

Event 15 September 2026

Materials for the Working Party for Schengen Matters included the Commission decision establishing the country report. ST 13022/26 is dated 14 September in the Council register; the meeting was scheduled for the 15th.

Why it matters

The document's progress into Council working bodies is confirmed. Inclusion in the materials alone does not establish adoption of a final decision.

Source and publication date

Source status: agenda and metadata. Council of the EU, meeting of 15.09.2026; register entry for ST 13022/26.

14JUL 2026ProcedureGrade ACommission adopts a positive country report

Event 14 July 2026

The Schengen Country Report of Cyprus 2025/2026 was adopted. According to the Commission, it is based on monitoring in December 2025 and gives a positive assessment of Cyprus's technical preparedness. The report was sent to the Council and the European Parliament.

Why it matters

The file advanced towards Council consideration. The Commission separately stressed that decisions on when and how accession takes place belong to the Council.

Source and publication date

Commission briefing dated 15.07.2026; ST 13022/26 entry referring to C(2026)3652. The September dates in the entries concern transmission of the materials, not the report's adoption in July.

European Commission · briefing of 15 July ST 13022/26 entry referring to C(2026)3652
26JUN 2026ProcedureGrade ASchengen Committee gives a positive opinion

Event 26 June 2026

Member states in the Schengen Committee gave a positive opinion on Cyprus's country report. The Commission later explicitly named this date at a briefing.

Why it matters

A stage preceding Commission adoption of the report was completed. This was not a unanimous Council decision removing checks.

Source and publication date

European Commission, briefing dated 15.07.2026, SCHENGEN — Cyprus section, retrospectively describing the opinion of 26.06.2026.

European Commission · briefing of 15 July
21MAY 2026PoliticsGrade B / CPresident shifts expected political decision to late 2026 or early 2027

Event 21 May 2026

Christodoulides reported substantial progress and said a political decision was expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

Why it matters

The public target became more cautious than the promise of accession in 2026. The political decision date and the date checks are actually removed may differ.

Source and publication date

Cyprus Presidency, statement of 21 May; KNEWS, report dated 21.05.2026.

President of Cyprus · statement of 21 May KNEWS, report dated 21.05.2026
18MAY 2026ProcedureGrade ACommission officially notes progress made in 2025

Event 18 May 2026

The State of Schengen Report 2026 confirmed substantial reforms in Cyprus and the December monitoring. Full accession remained an area of further EU work.

Why it matters

This was a positive assessment of progress in the general Schengen report. It preceded the separate country report on Cyprus.

Source and publication date

European Commission, COM(2026)150 final, 18.05.2026, section 3.3.

COM(2026)150 final, section 3.3
23JAN 2026ProcedureGrade B / CBrunner expects evaluation report adoption in spring

Event 23 January 2026

In an interview with CNA, the Commissioner reported substantial progress and expected the report to be adopted in spring 2026. Once readiness was confirmed, the Council would need to decide on accession unanimously.

Why it matters

Spring was the expected timing of a procedural step. Actual adoption of the report is confirmed on 14 July.

Source and publication date

CNA via ABNA-SE, Brunner interview, publication dated 23.01.2026; the exact recording day is not given.

CNA via ABNA-SE, Brunner interview
15JAN 2026PoliticsGrade BChristodoulides retains the 2026 accession target

Event 15 January 2026

At a joint press conference with Ursula von der Leyen, the President said readiness for full accession had been discussed and expressed an expectation of accession during the year.

Why it matters

The political goal remained after the December monitoring. The President's statement alone does not mean the Commission had agreed a legal date.

Source and publication date

Cyprus Presidency, statement at the joint press conference, 15.01.2026.

Cyprus Presidency, statement at the joint press conference
15DEC 2025PoliticsGrade BFrance and Cyprus prepare future consular representation

Event 15 December 2025

A letter of intent was signed in Paris for France to represent Cyprus in consular matters after full accession, where Cyprus has no presence of its own. The President thanked France for supporting accession in 2026.

Why it matters

A basis was prepared for future visa cooperation. The letter did not replace the readiness evaluation or the Council decision.

Source and publication date

Cyprus Presidency, announcement on the strategic partnership and Letter of Intent, event dated 15.12.2025; Greek announcement on the same day.

Cyprus Presidency, strategic partnership and Letter of Intent announcement Greek announcement on the same day
DEC2025Technical readinessGrade ACommission monitors readiness

Event December 2025

Monitoring activities assessed Cyprus's readiness after remedial work. They later formed the basis of the 2025/2026 country report adopted in July 2026.

Why it matters

This was actual verification following work on the recommendations. The primary sources cited do not give exact days, so the event is dated by month.

Source and publication date

COM(2026)150 final, section 3.3, 18.05.2026; European Commission briefing, 15.07.2026.

COM(2026)150 final, section 3.3 European Commission · briefing of 15 July
11MAY 2025PoliticsGrade B / CPresident names 2026 as the accession year

Event 11 May 2025

Christodoulides expressed confidence in accession in 2026. He expected technical preparations to be completed by the end of 2025, while seeking support from other countries and the European Parliament.

Why it matters

This statement named the accession year, whereas the January statement concerned technical readiness. The target imposed no binding deadline on the Council of the EU.

Source and publication date

CyBC, report dated 11.05.2025; CNA via StockWatch, English publication dated 12.05.2025 on the previous day's statement.

CyBC, report dated 11.05.2025 CNA via StockWatch
08MAY 2025ProcedureGrade A / BCabinet approves a VIS bill

Event 8 May 2025

The Council of Ministers approved a bill on the operation and use of the Visa Information System. It defined the national system, authorities' powers, access, application of visa rules, penalties and appeals.

Why it matters

Legislative preparation in the visa area advanced. Cabinet approval did not amount to parliamentary enactment or a confirmed launch of the European VIS.

Source and publication date

Official portal for the Cyprus government's programme, 08.05.2025.

Official portal for the Cyprus government’s programme
23APR 2025ProcedureGrade ACommission sets out a conditional path to verification visits

Event 23 April 2025

The State of Schengen Report 2025 noted improvements in return and SIS, but kept the initial evaluation open. Verification visits in 2025 depended on the necessary remedial work being completed beforehand.

Why it matters

A conditional route towards confirming readiness was published, without setting an accession date.

Source and publication date

European Commission, COM(2025)185 final with annexes, 23.04.2025.

European Commission, COM(2025)185 final with annexes
16APR 2025ProcedureGrade A / BCommission confirms the initial evaluation is continuing

Event 16 April 2025

In a reply to the European Parliament, Commissioner Magnus Brunner said Cyprus's initial Schengen evaluation was continuing. A positive result and a unanimous Council decision would be required, taking account of the island's special circumstances under Protocol No 10.

Why it matters

In spring 2025, the Commission had not yet declared the technical evaluation complete.

Source and publication date

European Parliament, reply to E-000502/2025, dated 16.04.2025, answering the question submitted on 05.02.2025.

European Parliament, reply to E-000502/2025
10JAN 2025PoliticsGrade BPresident sets a 2025 technical readiness target

Event 10 January 2025

At the Beyond Sea & Sun forum, Nikos Christodoulides announced a Foreign Ministry working group and the intention to meet technical conditions during 2025. In his assessment, political concerns related to the ceasefire line had been addressed.

Why it matters

The official text promised technical readiness in 2025. This was not a Council decision on accession in the same year.

Source and publication date

Cyprus Presidency, address at Beyond Sea & Sun; event and publication 10.01.2025.

Cyprus Presidency, address at Beyond Sea & Sun
19DEC 2024ProcedureGrade BGovernment reviews action plans across six areas

Event 19 December 2024

The Foreign Ministry held an interministerial meeting on data protection, police cooperation, borders, return, visas and SIS. Interior, justice, transport and migration authorities took part, and urgent tasks were identified.

Why it matters

Work continued across all evaluated areas. The announcement did not declare the plans closed.

Source and publication date

Cyprus Foreign Ministry, announcement on the interministerial meeting; event and publication 19.12.2024.

Cyprus Foreign Ministry, interministerial meeting announcement
13JUN 2024ProcedureGrade ACouncil calls for improvements to SIS use

Event 13 June 2024

The recommendations called for strengthening SIRENE, enabling the required alert categories, ensuring complete available data and object searches, and improving fingerprint use. An action plan was expected within two months, followed by reports every six months and a verification visit before closure.

Why it matters

Specific tasks on practical SIS use remained after connection.

Source and publication date

ST 11237/24, file 2024/0105(NLE), decision adopted 13.06.2024, final document dated 14.06.2024.

ST 11237/24
16APR 2024Technical readinessGrade ACommission reviews the first SIS results

Event 16 April 2024

The State of Schengen Report 2024 noted good integration of SIS into Cyprus's border, migration and police processes, but incomplete use of its potential. Since connection, about 20 people wanted under European Arrest Warrants had been arrested; roughly three quarters had been surrendered to the requesting states.

Why it matters

Measurable results of cooperation emerged. They did not mean preparation was complete in all areas.

Source and publication date

European Commission, COM(2024)173 final, 16.04.2024.

European Commission, COM(2024)173 final
20232–6 October 2023Technical readinessGrade APractical SIS use is evaluated

Event 2–6 October 2023

Following connection, the first evaluation of SIS application in Cyprus took place. The results were recorded in report C(2024)700. The Council later identified the SIRENE training centre and its set of instructions as good practice, but retained a list of improvements.

Why it matters

Launching the system made it possible to evaluate its actual use; technical connection did not complete the evaluation.

Source and publication date

ST 11237/24, document dated 14.06.2024, paragraph 1 gives the visit dates.

ST 11237/24
25JUL 2023Technical readinessGrade ACyprus connects to SIS in practice

Event 25 July 2023

Cypriot authorities began using SIS and entering their own alerts. The system enabled information exchange on wanted and missing people, certain categories of third-country nationals and stolen objects.

Why it matters

Practical integration into shared information exchange began. The Interior Ministry separately explained that border checks remained.

Source and publication date

eu-LISA, Cyprus fully integrated into SIS; European Commission in Cyprus; clarification by Cyprus's Interior Ministry, 25.07.2023.

eu-LISA, Cyprus fully integrated into SIS European Commission in Cyprus Cyprus Interior Ministry · SIS connection
13JUN 2023Technical readinessGrade AAuthorised SIS data transfer date arrives

Event 13 June 2023

From this date, the decision allowed SIS alerts, supplementary information and data to be made available to Cyprus. The main powers to use the system and enter its own alerts began on 25 July.

Why it matters

This was an intermediate legal launch date. It does not itself establish the exact day when each dataset was actually transferred.

Source and publication date

Source status: stage provided for in the act. Decision 2023/870, Article 1(2), act dated 25.04.2023.

25APR 2023ProcedureGrade ACouncil adopts decision applying SIS provisions

Event 25 April 2023

Decision 2023/870 was adopted. It provided for preparatory data transfer from 13 June and application of the relevant SIS rules from 25 July. Special restrictions remained until internal border checks were lifted.

Why it matters

This was legal authorisation for SIS integration. Full accession required a different decision.

Source and publication date

Council Decision 2023/870, adopted 25.04.2023, published 28.04.2023, entered into force 29.04.2023.

The Working Party for Schengen Matters, with associated countries participating, agreed the draft. Coreper endorsement and Council adoption were to follow.

The file moved towards adoption of the act, but working-level agreement did not itself open the system.

20137 October 2013 and 1 January 2016ProcedureGrade ANew evaluation mechanism provides a transition period for Cyprus

Event 7 October 2013 and 1 January 2016

Regulation 1053/2013 replaced the previous Schengen evaluation mechanism. It expressly recognised that Cyprus's evaluation had already begun under the old rules and deferred application of the new mechanism to Cyprus until 1 January 2016.

Why it matters

This provides the legal link between the early inspections and the modern procedure, rather than a new decision to admit Cyprus to Schengen.

Source and publication date

Regulation 1053/2013, recital 27 and Article 23; adopted 07.10.2013, published 06.11.2013.

Regulation 1053/2013
06DEC 2007ProcedureGrade ACouncil admits nine countries from the 2004 enlargement, excluding Cyprus

Event 6 December 2007

Decision 2007/801/EC extended full application of the rules to Czechia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Malta, Poland, Slovenia and Slovakia. Land and sea checks were to end on 21 December 2007 and air checks on 30 March 2008. Cyprus was not listed.

Why it matters

Cyprus's path diverged from that of the other nine countries that joined the EU in 2004. Its absence from the list alone establishes neither a single cause of delay nor a veto by any country.

Source and publication date

Decision 2007/801/EC, adopted 06.12.2007, published 08.12.2007.

Decision 2007/801/EC
21SEP 2007ProcedureGrade ACommission links Green Line surveillance to future Schengen participation

Event 21 September 2007

In its Green Line report, the Commission urged Cyprus to fulfil its surveillance obligations with future Schengen participation in mind. At the same time, it maintained the approach of avoiding excessive obstacles to contacts between communities and not treating the line as an EU external border.

Why it matters

The practical question of monitoring the line was already on the official agenda at an early stage.

Source and publication date

European Commission, COM(2007)553 final, 21.09.2007.

20NOV 2006Technical readinessGrade ADraft conclusions list problems after the early inspections

Event 20 November 2006

The draft recorded that sea and air border evaluations had not yet taken place. The data protection authority lacked resources and experience with SIS, and a revisit was needed. Database and SIRENE bureau tasks remained in police cooperation.

Why it matters

Progress was partial. The document cannot be presented as an accession decision or finally adopted Council conclusions.

Source and publication date

Source status: working draft. ST 14518/2/06 REV 2, 20.11.2006, pp. 3–4. Wording in other draft versions on the ‘border issue’ does not establish a legal requirement to reunify the island first.

Council of the EU, ST 14518/2/06 REV 2
20052005 and 1 May 2006ProcedureGrade AEarly readiness declaration opens a partial evaluation

Event 2005 and 1 May 2006

Cyprus's declaration was registered as 7555/05 SCHEVAL18 COMIX192. It allowed evaluation to start from 1 May 2006, with airports, seaports and visa issuance deferred. On-site inspections of police cooperation and data protection took place.

Why it matters

Official Schengen evaluation existed long before 2019. The date 1 May refers to the start of the early stage, rather than completion of the inspections.

Source and publication date

Council of the EU, ST 14518/2/06 REV 2, 20.11.2006, paragraphs 10–11. The public copy was declassified in 2018; that is the disclosure date of an older source. The exact submission day of the 2005 declaration is not established in this entry.

Council of the EU, ST 14518/2/06 REV 2
01MAY 2004ProcedureGrade ACyprus joins the EU with border checks retained

Event 1 May 2004

Cyprus became an EU member, and the Act of Accession obligations took effect. Full application of the Schengen package and removal of the relevant checks remained subject to a separate procedure.

Why it matters

EU membership did not mean automatic entry into the area without internal border checks.

Source and publication date

Act of Accession, Article 3; European Parliament, 2012 overview, p. 24.

29APR 2004ProcedureGrade ACouncil establishes a special Green Line regime

Event 29 April 2004

Regulation 866/2004 was adopted on movement of people and goods across the line between government-controlled areas and areas outside its effective control. It took effect on 1 May. The Green Line was not recognised as an ordinary EU external border.

Why it matters

A special legal regime was created that must be taken into account in the island's Schengen integration.

Source and publication date

Regulation 866/2004, corrected official text, adopted 29.04.2004; corrected publication 09.06.2004. European Commission explanation.

05NOV 2003Technical readinessGrade APre-accession monitoring leaves SIS, airport and data-protection tasks

Event 5 November 2003

The final monitoring report assessed preparation under the plan as satisfactory for EU accession. Integration into SIS II, separation of passenger flows at airports and ports, and strengthening the Data Protection Commissioner's office still remained.

Why it matters

The Commission distinguished readiness for EU membership from meeting the conditions for future removal of internal checks.

Source and publication date

European Commission, SEC(2003)1202 final, Chapter 24; European Parliament register giving the report date as 05.11.2003.

European Commission, SEC(2003)1202 final European Parliament register giving the report date as 05.11.2003
16APR 2003ProcedureGrade AAccession treaty establishes a two-stage Schengen model

Event 16 April 2003

Article 3 of the Act of Accession provided for some Schengen provisions to apply from EU membership. The remaining provisions also became binding, but their application required a separate Council decision after verification of the conditions and consultation of the European Parliament.

Why it matters

The legal basis for later accession was established. The treaty set no calendar deadline for removing checks.

Source and publication date

2003 Act of Accession, Article 3; the treaty was signed on 16.04.2003 and published in OJ L236 on 23.09.2003.

2003 Act of Accession, Article 3
09OCT 2002Technical readinessGrade ACommission records SIS delays and port-control problems

Event 9 October 2002

The regular report confirmed implementation of the Schengen Action Plan and airport preparations. Developments in SIS II were delaying some IT measures. Embarkation and disembarkation procedures at seaports still did not fully ensure the required individual checks on people crossing the border.

Why it matters

Having a plan did not mean readiness was complete. Preparation already depended on infrastructure, IT and the work of border services together.

Source and publication date

European Commission, SEC(2002)1401, 09.10.2002, printed pp. 104 and 131. The dates for future terminals in the document were plans at that time.

European Commission, SEC(2002)1401
DEC2001ProcedureGrade AChapter 24 is provisionally closed

Event December 2001

The justice and home affairs negotiating chapter was provisionally closed. In the final factsheet after the negotiations ended, its final status is dated December 2002. No transitional periods were provided for the chapter.

Why it matters

The parties agreed the EU accession terms for this chapter. Removing checks between Cyprus and Schengen countries remained a separate future stage.

Source and publication date

European Parliament, WIP/2002/11/0037, p. 1; the document gives both closure dates.

European Parliament, Cyprus — Chapter 24, WIP/2002/11/0037
MAY2001Technical readinessGrade ACyprus adopts a Schengen Action Plan

Event May 2001

Cyprus approved a plan to implement Schengen rules. Plans for Larnaca and Paphos airports were changed to separate passenger flows, and equipment to detect forged documents was installed in the summer. National SIS equipment, coastal radar, patrol boats and helicopters were planned for 2001–2002.

Why it matters

Preparation gained a specific plan and infrastructure tasks. The future purchases listed in the report did not yet represent completed work.

Source and publication date

European Commission, SEC(2001)1745, report dated 13.11.2001, printed p. 79.

European Commission, SEC(2001)1745
MAY2000ProcedureGrade AJustice and home affairs negotiating chapter opens

Event May 2000

Chapter 24 of Cyprus's EU accession negotiations opened. It included Schengen rules on borders, visas, data protection and police cooperation. The European Parliament separately explained that EU accession would not automatically remove checks: a subsequent unanimous Council decision would be needed.

Why it matters

Formal negotiations began on the package that included Schengen. This was part of the EU membership negotiations, rather than a separate decision on Schengen accession.

Source and publication date

European Parliament, Cyprus — Chapter 24, WIP/2002/11/0037, p. 1; a retrospective factsheet after the negotiations ended. It gives the opening month, without a day.

European Parliament, Cyprus — Chapter 24, WIP/2002/11/0037
13OCT 1999ProcedureGrade ACommission explicitly includes Schengen in Cyprus's preparations

Event 13 October 1999

In its regular report, the Commission called for adoption of the Schengen visa system, document checks aligned with the Schengen Convention and preparation of government computer networks for SIS. Personal data protection remained a separate area of work.

Why it matters

This is a documented starting point for the timeline: substantive preparation was under way by 1999. The report does not establish the date of the first political discussion.

Source and publication date

1999 Regular Report on Cyprus’ progress towards accession, cover date 13.10.1999, printed pp. 39–40 and 57–58. The footer ‘First Draft 06/10/99’ refers to an internal version of the text.
